title: The person's integration catalog and connected accounts, read live from each tool

provider_id.description: apple is the Apple (iCloud) tile: its services are ordinary imap, caldav and carddav accounts, which carry apple_id. gitea is the Gitea tile: its connections are tea's native logins, listed under gitea, never under accounts. gitlab is the GitLab tile (gitlab.com or a self-hosted GitLab): its connections are glab's native host logins, listed under gitlab. atlassian and trello are native Pi MCP connections: the address is the native server name, and trello may have several (open_habitat_trello, open_habitat_trello_2 …), each its own Pi sign-in.

level.description: An account level: a boundary the provider itself enforces, so it holds against an agent running as the person. full is everything the catalog asks; nosend (Microsoft) is everything but sending mail: mail is read, organised and drafted, and calendars, contacts and files are changed, though a calendar change still sends invitations and a file grant can create a sharing link; drafts (Microsoft) reads and drafts mail but never sends, and reads calendars, contacts and files, so the account sends nothing; read reads only, and its files are a one-way mirror; app_folder (Dropbox) is full access to the application's own folder (Apps/<application>) alone. A Microsoft level is one of the operator's Entra applications, a Dropbox level the App folder application or the Full Dropbox one asked for reading only, and a Google level the scope set the one application asks for (Google has no drafts level: its drafts scope sends too).

skill.description: The generated personal-data skill: current, none (no accounts), blocked (a file the host did not write occupies its path) or failed (could not be written).

available.description: False when the tool is not installed or the operator has not configured the application.

unavailable_reason.description: Present only when unavailable: app_credentials_required when the tools are installed and only the operator's application registration is missing, tool_unavailable otherwise.

missing_tools.description: With tool_unavailable only: the catalog's tools this installation does not provide as trusted executables, in the entry's order.

accounts_unreadable.description: Present, and true, when the tool's own account files could not be read safely (for example a directory on their path is writable by others or is a link): this provider's accounts are missing from accounts because they could not be listed, not because there are none. The other providers are listed as usual.

login.description: personal_token is the Gitea and GitLab form: an address and a personal access token the daemon validates and writes only into tea's or glab's own login file.

levels.description: Present for a provider whose sign-in chooses an account level, broadest first: each level it shows and whether it can be chosen. A level that is not available is shown but cannot be chosen, and reason says why: application_missing, the server's administrator has not registered the application it needs; not_offered, the provider has no boundary for it (Google's drafts level), shown so the choice is honest.

state.description: unknown is a check that could not find the state out. pending_first_sync is a service not checked while a first sync of the same provider runs (this account's or another's): its tool shares that sync's native credentials, so it is checked after the sync.

failure.description: Why a sync_failed service stopped or why a sync_restarting service's latest pass failed; the native login is retained. quota_insufficient and quota_unavailable are an initial-inventory admission refusal before anything was copied, shown until the person chooses again (also after a daemon restart) on a files service whose first pass never ran or never finished; initial_sync_incomplete is a working login whose first sync never finished and is not being resumed (signing in again offers the initial choice); not_chosen is a working login whose files never had a first pass, because the person left them out or the first choice was refused before anything was copied (signing in again offers the choice); initial_sync_resume_failed is a first sync that a daemon stop interrupted, whose automatic resume then failed. needs_resync is a critical abort only an explicit resync recovers: on sync_failed the native listings were set aside (signing in again is not the remedy), on sync_restarting the latest pass said so. Also on sync_restarting: delete_limit is bisync's mass-deletion safeguard, all_changed its safeguard against a pass in which every file of a side changed (the daemon resumes that pass itself once a fresh check finds no mass deletion), remote_unreachable a pass that could not reach the provider and pass_failed any other failed pass. A pass failure stays until a pass succeeds. On login_expired, every service of an account whose native configuration could not follow the operator's current application carries the reason: app_changed when it was signed in with another application, tenant_changed when the application's tenant refused its grant (signing in again is the remedy for both), outside_tenant when the account is not in that tenant's directory (signing in again cannot help).

needed_bytes.description: With quota_insufficient, when known: the counted size of the chosen files that did not fit. It is kept, like the refusal itself, until the person chooses again, also across a daemon restart.

free_bytes.description: With needed_bytes: the room the chosen files did not fit, when they were counted.

last_synced_at.description: When the latest successful sync pass ended, from the tool's own committed listings; for several libraries, the oldest. Absent before the first pass has finished.

access.description: What the provider's grant lets this service do, read from the grant itself and never from a record of what was asked: full is everything the catalog asks of it, or any grant that sends mail (a level never claims less than the token can do), drafts is mail that can be read and drafted but not sent, read is reading only, none is a service the grant leaves out, which nothing reaches (its state is then unknown). A file service syncs both ways with full; with read they are a one-way mirror whose local changes never reach the provider and are overwritten. Absent when the account's grant cannot be read now, and for accounts without one (app passwords).

scope.description: A permission in the provider's own name: a Google scope, a Microsoft Graph permission or a Dropbox scope.

grant.description: The provider's grant as the daemon read it now: from gog's store of the token's scopes (Google), the tenant's answer to the Outlook tool's refresh (Microsoft) or the scopes the sign-in's token response named, kept beside the token in rclone's config (Dropbox). not_granted lists what the catalog asks for that the grant lacks: left out on the consent page, or not consented to by the organisation. Identity scopes are not listed.

sync_progress.description: Transient native rclone current-pass stats: the initial pass on a syncing service, an ordinary pass running now on an ok or sync_restarting one. Totals may change while listing and reset between Microsoft libraries. No messages or filenames.

gitea_connection_id.description: Derived by the daemon from tea's login name, canonical base and user; it carries no token material and selects nothing the daemon did not observe itself.

gitea_base_url.description: A canonical HTTPS Gitea base: lowercase host, port only when not 443, base path without a trailing slash. Never userinfo, query or fragment.

gitea_git.description: Git readiness, observed from the person's own Git configuration without the network: registered (the credential helper answers for this base), absent, foreign (another helper or setting owns the scope), shadowed (a later helper entry answers first) or unknown (Git could not be asked).

gitea_connection.description: One of tea's native logins, read from its file alone. base_url and user are present only when tea's entry carries a valid HTTPS address and user. Only a pat that is not ambiguous can be used.

kind.description: pat is a token login the connector can use; oauth, ssh, insecure and invalid entries are shown, never used or rewritten.

owned.description: The connector created this entry; otherwise the person made it with tea or by hand.

ambiguous.description: Another entry has the same name or the same base and user; neither is used until the person resolves it in tea.

gitea.description: tea's native logins as the daemon read them now. unavailable: tea's file is unsafe, malformed or unreadable, which is never an empty list.

gitlab_connection_id.description: Derived by the daemon from glab's hosts key, canonical base and user; it carries no token material and selects nothing the daemon did not observe itself.

gitlab_full_name.description: A GitLab project path: the namespace (a user, or a group and up to 19 subgroups) and the project, group/subgroup/.../project, 2 to 21 segments, shown in full. Never a dot segment, GitLab's route separator - or a segment ending in .git or .atom.

gitlab_connection.description: One of glab's signed-in host logins, read from its file alone; glab keeps one per server. base_url and user are present only when glab's entry names a valid HTTPS server and user. Only a pat that is not ambiguous can be used.

kind.description: pat is a token in glab's file the connector can use; oauth (glab refreshes it), keyring (the token is in the operating system's keyring), insecure (glab is told to skip or replace TLS verification, use a proxy, add headers or speak HTTP) and invalid entries are shown, never used or rewritten.

ambiguous.description: Another of glab's host keys names the same server; neither is used until the person removes one.

gitlab.description: glab's signed-in host logins as the daemon read them now. unavailable: glab's file is unsafe, malformed or unreadable, which is never an empty list.

apple_id.description: Present when the account's stored server is Apple's iCloud: the Apple ID whose card shows it. A mail account's address is its iCloud Mail address, which may differ.

level.description: The account level its grant amounts to, read from the grant and never from what was chosen: Microsoft's and Google's from the services' access, Dropbox's from the application and the grant. Absent when the grant cannot be read now or an organisation narrowed it to none of the levels; the services then say what it allows.
